1.web: Oh that you were like my brother, who nursed from the breasts of my mother! If I found you outside, I would kiss you; yes, and no one would despise me.
1.asv: Oh that thou wert as my brother, That sucked the breasts of my mother! WhenI should find thee without, I would kiss thee; Yea, and none would despise me.

2.web: I would lead you, bringing you into my mother’s house, who would instruct me. I would have you drink spiced wine, of the juice of my pomegranate.
2.asv: I would lead thee, and bring thee into my mother’s house, Who would instruct me; I would cause thee to drink of spiced wine, Of the juice of my pomegranate.

3.web: His left hand would be under my head. His right hand would embrace me.
3.asv: His left handshould beunder my head, And his right hand should embrace me.

4.web: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, that you not stir up, nor awaken love, until it so desires. Friends
4.asv: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, That ye stir not up, nor awake my love, Until he please.

5.web: Who is this who comes up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved? Under the apple tree I aroused you. There your mother conceived you. There she was in labor and bore you.
5.asv: Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness, Leaning upon her beloved? Under the apple-tree I awakened thee: There thy mother was in travail with thee, There was she in travail that brought thee forth.

6.web: Set me as a seal on your heart, as a seal on your arm; for love is strong as death. Jealousy is as cruel as Sheol. Its flashes are flashes of fire, a very flame of Yahweh.
6.asv: Set me as a seal upon thy heart, As a seal upon thine arm: For love is strong as death; Jealousy is cruel as Sheol; The flashes thereof are flashes of fire, A very flame of Jehovah.

7.web: Many waters can’t quench love, neither can floods drown it. If a man would give all the wealth of his house for love, he would be utterly scorned. Friends
7.asv: Many waters cannot quench love, Neither can floods drown it: If a man would give all the substance of his house for love, He would utterly be contemned.

8.web: We have a little sister. She has no breasts. What shall we do for our sister in the day when she is to be spoken for?
8.asv: We have a little sister, And she hath no breasts: What shall we do for our sister In the day when she shall be spoken for?

9.web: If she is a wall, we will build on her a turret of silver. if she is a door, we will enclose her with boards of cedar. Beloved
9.asv: If she be a wall, We will build upon her a turret of silver: And if she be a door, We will inclose her with boards of cedar.

10.web: I am a wall, and my breasts like towers, then I was in his eyes like one who found peace.
10.asv: I am a wall, and my breasts like the towersthereof Then was I in his eyes as one that found peace.

11.web: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal Hamon. He leased out the vineyard to keepers. Each was to bring a thousand shekels of silver for its fruit.
11.asv: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon; He let out the vineyard unto keepers; Every one for the fruit thereof was to bring a thousand pieces of silver.

12.web: My own vineyard is before me. The thousand are for you, Solomon; two hundred for those who tend its fruit. Lover
12.asv: My vineyard, which is mine, is before me: Thou, O Solomon, shalt have the thousand, And those that keep the fruit thereof two hundred.

13.web: You who dwell in the gardens, with friends in attendance, let me hear your voice! Beloved
13.asv: Thou that dwellest in the gardens, The companions hearken for thy voice: Cause me to hear it.

14.web: Come away, my beloved! Be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of spices!
14.asv: Make haste, my beloved, And be thou like to a roe or to a young hart Upon the mountains of spices.
